<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Infant Cereal Ingredients, flour or meal from conventional had lead higher at 8,730 µg/kg, against 2,070 µg/kg for ecological in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Slepecka K, Kalwa K, Wyrostek J, Pankiewicz U · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland">Evaluation of cadmium, lead, zinc and copper levels in selected ecological cereal food products and their non-ecological counterparts</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Current Issues in Pharmacy and Medical Sciences 30(3):147-150</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/bfr2018-infant-food-cadmium-lead|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment (BfR) · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bfr2018-infant-food-cadmium-lead">EU maximum levels for cadmium in food for infants and young children sufficient - For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the infant Cereal Ingredients came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-infant-cereal-ingredients" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-infant-cereal-ingredients-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of infant cereal ingredients, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>1</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for infant cereal ingredients, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>WHO GEMS/Food is the only compatible sampling family for infant cereal ingredients, as sold on this basis in the completed infant cereal ingredients ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach infant Cereal Ingredients

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach infant Cereal Ingredients comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Infant Cereal Ingredients, flour or meal from ecological had cadmium higher at 12,300 µg/kg, against 120 µg/kg for conventional in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Slepecka K, Kalwa K, Wyrostek J, Pankiewicz U · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland">Evaluation of cadmium, lead, zinc and copper levels in selected ecological cereal food products and their non-ecological counterparts</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Current Issues in Pharmacy and Medical Sciences 30(3):147-150</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>

<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>
## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="hmi-ing-022"></a>
<a id="can-an-intervention-increase-another-contaminant-or-redistribute-contamination-to-a-by-product"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>
<a id="what-effects-on-nutrition-yield-sensory-quality-stability-and-waste-streams-were-measured"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Slepecka K, Kalwa K, Wyrostek J, Pankiewicz U · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland">Evaluation of cadmium, lead, zinc and copper levels in selected ecological cereal food products and their non-ecological counterparts</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Current Issues in Pharmacy and Medical Sciences 30(3):147-150</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into infant Cereal Ingredients?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, infant Cereal Ingredients from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than infant Cereal Ingredients from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Slepecka K, Kalwa K, Wyrostek J, Pankiewicz U · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland">Evaluation of cadmium, lead, zinc and copper levels in selected ecological cereal food products and their non-ecological counterparts</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Current Issues in Pharmacy and Medical Sciences 30(3):147-150</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Infant Cereal Ingredients, flour or meal from conventional had lead higher at 8,730 µg/kg, against 2,070 µg/kg for ecological in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Slepecka K, Kalwa K, Wyrostek J, Pankiewicz U · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland">Evaluation of cadmium, lead, zinc and copper levels in selected ecological cereal food products and their non-ecological counterparts</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Current Issues in Pharmacy and Medical Sciences 30(3):147-150</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
